name: Visual Genome
description: Visual Genome is a dataset designed to enable comprehensive scene understanding by connecting language and vision. It contains 108,249 images densely annotated with region descriptions, objects, attributes, relationships, scene graphs, and question-answer pairs. Each image has an average of 21 objects, 18 attributes, 18 relationships, 42 region descriptions, and 17 question-answer pairs. The dataset aims to bridge the gap between perceptual tasks (like object detection) and cognitive tasks (like image description and question answering) by providing structured, formalized representations of images in the form of scene graphs.
creator: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bernstein, Li Fei-Fei (Stanford University, Dresden University of Technology, Yahoo Inc., Snapchat Inc.)
citeAs: Ranjay Krishna et al. Visual Genome: Connecting Language and Vision Using Crowdsourced Dense Image Annotations. arXiv:1602.07332v1 [cs.CV] 23 Feb 2016
rai:dataCollection: The Visual Genome dataset uses 108,249 images from the intersection of the YFCC100M and MS-COCO datasets. These images are real-world, non-iconic images uploaded to Flickr by users. The dataset was collected over 6 months after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation. Data collection involved multiple stages: (1) region descriptions with bounding boxes, (2) object extraction from descriptions with bounding boxes, (3) attribute and relationship extraction, (4) region graph construction, (5) scene graph creation by merging region graphs, and (6) question-answer pair collection (both freeform and region-based).
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images were sourced from the intersection of YFCC100M (100 million Flickr images) and MS-COCO (328,000 images), resulting in 108,249 real-world, non-iconic images. Images range from 72 to 1280 pixels wide, with an average width of 500 pixels.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The dataset was collected over 6 months (after 15 months of experimentation), with data collection occurring in 2015-2016 based on the paper submission date of February 2016.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For region descriptions: BLEU score thresholds (0.7) were enforced to ensure diversity and prevent repetition of descriptions both within an image and globally across the dataset. For objects: Stanford's dependency parser was used to automatically extract nouns as suggestions to speed up the process. For attributes and relationships: text was lowercased, lemmatized, and excess whitespace was stripped. Random sampling of 500 instances per category was performed when a category had more than 500 examples. For canonicalization: All objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases were mapped to WordNet synsets using WordNet lexeme counts, with 15-30 hand-crafted mapping rules to address common failure cases.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: All annotations were collected via Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) with over 33,000 unique workers contributing over 800,000 HITs. Workers were paid to earn $6-$8 per hour. Region descriptions: Workers drew bounding boxes and wrote descriptions, with each image receiving 50 region descriptions collected iteratively. Workers were shown the top 7 most similar previous descriptions (calculated using BLEU scores) to encourage diversity. Objects: Workers extracted objects from region descriptions and drew tight bounding boxes satisfying coverage (box covers all mentioned objects) and quality (box is as tight as possible, within 4 pixels). Attributes and relationships: Workers added attributes to objects and connected object pairs with relationships based on region description text. Question-answer pairs: Workers wrote QA pairs following three rules: (1) start with one of the seven Ws, (2) avoid ambiguous/speculative questions, (3) be precise and unique. Eight freeform QAs were collected per image (requiring at least 3 different Ws), and region-based QAs were collected for regions with large areas (>5k pixels) and long phrases (>4 words). All annotations went through verification using either majority voting (3 workers, 2/3 agreement required) or rapid judgments for objects.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Verification was conducted using two strategies: (1) Majority voting for region descriptions, attributes, relationships, and QAs - three unique workers voted on each annotation, requiring at least 2/3 agreement for inclusion. (2) Rapid judgments for objects - using an interface inspired by rapid serial visual processing to verify objects with an order of magnitude increase in speed compared to majority voting. The dataset achieved a 94.1% retention rate, meaning 94.1% of workers who completed one task went on to do more.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each image has an average of 42 region descriptions (each with a bounding box), 21 objects (each with a bounding box), 16 attributes, 18 relationships, and 17 question-answer pairs. For verification, each annotation received votes from 3 workers in the majority voting process.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 33,000 unique workers contributed from AMT. Geographic distribution: 93.02% from United States, 1.29% Philippines, 1.13% Kenya, 0.94% India, 0.50% Russia, 0.47% Canada, 2.65% others. Age distribution: majority between 25-34 years old, youngest contributor 18 years old, oldest 68 years old. Gender distribution: 54.15% male, 45.85% female.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford NLP tools (Stanford CoreNLP) were used to extract noun phrases from region descriptions and QAs, and to automatically extract nouns as suggestions during object extraction (achieving 99% recall on a subset of 200 manually annotated region descriptions). WordNet was used for canonicalization, mapping all objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases to synsets.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains human attributes including gender (man, woman, boy, girl, person), age-related attributes (young, old, teenager), physical attributes (tall, skinny, fit), emotional states (happy, angry), and activities/poses (standing, walking, skiing, surfing). Geographic and cultural information may be implicit in image content.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is biased towards images of people, as shown in the top synsets (ski, ballplayer, racket - all referring to people playing sports). The image source (Flickr) introduces biases toward certain types of content. The authors note that certain sports (skiing, surfboarding) are overrepresented due to bias in the image sources. The dataset uses images from MS-COCO and YFCC100M, which may carry their own inherent biases. The canonicalization process achieved varying precision rates: 86% for objects, 83.5% for attributes, and 77.6% for relationships, indicating some systematic errors in semantic mapping.
rai:dataLimitations: The authors acknowledge several limitations: (1) Canonicalization is not perfect and contains some ambiguity, with mapping accuracies of 86% for objects, 83.5% for attributes, and 77.6% for relationships. (2) The heuristic for merging co-referenced objects (0.8 intersection over union threshold) might contain false positives. (3) Relationship prediction experiments showed low accuracy (8.74% top-1) due to high intra-class variability, indicating relationships are not visually distinct enough for discriminative models to learn effectively. (4) Region description generation models showed objectively low accuracy (43.03% human judgment for Visual Genome-trained model), illustrating that current models are unable to reason about complex images. (5) The dataset is somewhat biased towards images of people and certain sports activities.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for training and benchmarking models for comprehensive scene understanding tasks including: (1) Object detection and classification, (2) Attribute prediction and classification, (3) Relationship prediction and classification, (4) Dense image captioning and region description generation, (5) Visual question answering, (6) Semantic image retrieval using scene graphs, (7) Image understanding evaluation, (8) Visual relationship extraction, (9) Action recognition, (10) Spatial reasoning between objects. The paper provides baseline experiments for attribute prediction, relationship prediction, region description generation, and question answering. The dataset can be used for both training (80% split mentioned in experiments) and testing/validation (10% each).
